title: Design principles: Taste starts arguments. Principles end them.

hero.sub: The five rules Night Ace designs by

slides.tail: The five rules Night Ace designs by.

slides.title: Why principles
slides.body: Debates about how something looks can run forever. Debates about a rule end quickly. A principle is a design decision you make once — then reuse on every screen that follows.

slides.title: One job per screen
slides.body: Every screen gets one job, and the layout should make it obvious. When everything is bold, nothing is.

slides.title: Whitespace is structure
slides.body: Empty space isn't wasted space — it's how readers know what belongs together. Crowded layouts push that work onto the visitor.

slides.title:
Type does the
heavy lifting
slides.body: Most of an interface is text. Get the type right — size, spacing, contrast — and the design is mostly finished before a single decoration appears.

slides.title: Consistency beats novelty
slides.body: The second time a pattern appears, it should look exactly like the first. People learn an interface once; don't make them relearn it on every page.

slides.title: Everything earns its place
slides.body: If removing an element changes nothing, it was decoration. Remove things until something breaks, then put only that one thing back.

slides.title: Designed on purpose
slides.body: Principles are why a design survives contact with real content. Want a site designed on purpose? Send Night Ace a message — we'll show you our reasoning, not just our portfolio.
